==> .claude/rules/api-test.md <==
---
description: API calls for test-data setup — the endpoint registry and known endpoint quirks
globs: core/api/**/*.ts,fixtures/**/*.ts,tests/helpers/**/*.ts,tests/specs/**/helpers/**/*.ts,utils/constants/routes.ts
alwaysApply: false
paths:
  - "core/api/**/*.ts"
  - "fixtures/**/*.ts"
  - "tests/helpers/**/*.ts"
  - "tests/specs/**/helpers/**/*.ts"
  - "utils/constants/routes.ts"
---

# API calls for test-data setup: invariants

The specs test the UI. The API prepares the test data: customers, basket contents, addresses, cards and the wallet balance.
This file contains only the facts that are always true.

## The registry

- Every endpoint that the code calls is in `docs/references/endpoints.csv`.
- If an endpoint is not in the registry, stop. Report that it is missing. Do not invent a path.
- Put each path into `utils/constants/routes.ts`. API clients in `core/api/` use these constants.

## Known API quirks

| Endpoint | Quirk |
|---|---|
| POST /api/Addresss | The path has three `s`. The app code uses this name |
| POST /rest/user/login | The response body is `{ authentication: { token, bid, umail } }`. `bid` is the basket id |
| POST /rest/user/login | Wrong credentials → **401** |
| PUT /rest/wallet/balance | Needs a saved card of the customer. Without a card → **402** `Payment not accepted.` |
| POST /api/BasketItems, PUT /api/BasketItems/:id | A quantity over the purchase limit → **400** |
| Basket, basket items, addresses, cards, wallet, order history | Need the header `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. The server does not read the token from a cookie |

## ❌ Forbidden

```
NEVER hardcode endpoint paths ('/api/...', '/rest/...'). Use the constants in utils/constants/routes.ts.
NEVER use relative imports (../../). Use @/ path aliases.
NEVER reuse the same customer across tests in parallel workers.
NEVER call an endpoint that is not in docs/references/endpoints.csv.
```

==> .claude/rules/auth-and-sessions.md <==
---
description: Customer auth — authenticate() API session, UI login only when the login screen is under test
globs: tests/**/*.ts,tests/**/*.spec.ts,page-objects/login-page.ts,fixtures/**/*.ts
alwaysApply: false
paths:
  - "tests/**/*.ts"
  - "tests/**/*.spec.ts"
  - "page-objects/login-page.ts"
  - "fixtures/**/*.ts"
---

# Auth and sessions

Do not log in through the UI. The only exception: the test checks the login screen itself.

## Two methods — do not confuse them

| Method | What it does | When |
|---|---|---|
| `loginPage.authenticate(customer)` | Gets a token through `POST /rest/user/login`. Puts the session into the browser. Opens the app as a logged-in customer. | Every spec that needs a logged-in customer |
| `loginPage.login(email, password)` | A real UI login. It fills the form, clicks `Log in` and waits for the redirect. | Only when the login screen is under test |

## How the app keeps the session

The frontend of v20.3.0 (`login.component.ts`) keeps the session in three places after a login:

| Place | Key | Value |
|---|---|---|
| `localStorage` | `token` | `authentication.token` from the login response |
| cookie | `token` | the same token |
| `sessionStorage` | `bid` | `authentication.bid`, the basket id of the customer |

`authenticate()` puts these three values into the browser before the app loads. Without `bid`, the basket of the customer does not load.

**Do not use `storageState`.** Playwright `storageState` does not save `sessionStorage`. The basket id is lost.

## Which pattern to use when

| Scenario | Pattern |
|----------|---------|
| A new customer for each test | `createCustomer(api)` → `loginPage.authenticate(customer)`, in a helper or a fixture |
| A customer with a prepared basket, address or card | API setup in a helper (`api-test.md`) → `loginPage.authenticate(customer)` |
| Switching customers in the middle of a test | `loginPage.authenticate(otherCustomer)` |
| Testing the **login screen** itself (fields, errors, redirect) | `loginPage.open()` + `loginPage.login()`. This is the **only** place where a UI login is allowed. |

## ✅ Right — new customer

```ts
test('with a new customer', async ({ api, loginPage, basketPage }) => {
  const customer = await createCustomer(api);
  await loginPage.authenticate(customer);
  await basketPage.open();
  await basketPage.shouldSeePage();
});
```

## ✅ Right — testing the login page

```ts
test('error on wrong password', async ({ api, loginPage }) => {
  const customer = await createCustomer(api);
  await loginPage.open();
  await loginPage.login(customer.email, 'wrong-password');
  await loginPage.shouldSeeInvalidCredentialsError();
});
```

## ❌ Wrong

```ts
test.use({ storageState: 'state.json' });                 // sessionStorage (bid) is lost
await loginPage.login(customer.email, customer.password); // UI login outside a login-screen test
```

==> .claude/rules/autotest-tags.md <==
---
description: Playwright tags — dictionary values only
globs: tests/specs/**/*.spec.ts
alwaysApply: false
paths:
  - "tests/specs/**/*.spec.ts"
---

# Playwright tags

## 1) The dictionary

- Take tags **only** from `AUTOTEST_PLAYWRIGHT_TAGS` in `utils/constants/autotest-labels.ts`.
- The dictionary holds these values: `@auth`, `@cart`, `@coupon`, `@checkout`, `@wallet`.
- If the file does not exist, create it with these values.

```ts
export const AUTOTEST_PLAYWRIGHT_TAGS = {
  auth: '@auth',
  cart: '@cart',
  coupon: '@coupon',
  checkout: '@checkout',
  wallet: '@wallet',
} as const;
```

## 2) Where the tag goes

- Put filter tags into `test.describe(..., { tag: [...] }, ...)` or `test(..., { tag: [...] }, ...)`.
- A tag must not repeat the path. Example: a test in `coupon/` gets no extra tag only because of the folder name.
- Use two tags only for a test that really crosses areas. Do not use them as a copy of the folder structure.
- Put the tag on `describe` when there is one. In files without `describe`, put it on every `test(...)`.

## 3) Forbidden

- Do not put raw strings directly into `tag: [...]`.
- Do not create per-file label dictionaries.

==> .claude/rules/code-quality.md <==
---
description: Code quality anti-patterns and clean code
globs: "**/*.{ts,tsx,js,jsx}"
alwaysApply: false
paths:
  - "**/*.{ts,tsx,js,jsx}"
---

# Code Quality — anti-patterns and clean code

## Project anti-patterns (forbidden)

| Anti-pattern | Correct |
|-------------|-----------|
| `loginPage.open()` + `login()` in regression specs | `loginPage.authenticate(customer)`, or a fixture that does it |
| One customer for several tests | A new customer inside each `test()` (`test-user-lifecycle.md`) |
| A customer created inside a `for` loop at test declaration time | Create it **inside** `test()` |
| `expect()` in `tests/specs/**` | `should*` methods in POM and helpers |
| `new BasketApiClient()` or raw API calls in `test()` | A fixture or a domain helper |
| `waitForTimeout` / `this.wait()` in POM | A locator plus `toBeVisible` or `toPass` |
| `networkidle` on reload or navigate | `domcontentloaded` plus an explicit wait for an anchor element |
| `any` in production code (`core/`, `page-objects/`, `utils/`) | Generics `<T = unknown>` or concrete interfaces |
| A hard-coded email or password in a spec | A generated value from the customer helper |
| God file over ~300 lines | Split into components or domain specs |

## General anti-patterns

### God Object
One class does everything. Split it into services, components and helpers.

### Hardcoded Values
Replace magic numbers and strings with constants, enums or `DateHelper` calls.

### Copy-Paste
Put shared logic into helpers (`tests/helpers/`, `utils/helpers/`).

### Overengineering
Keep the code simple. Do not build extra layers for a single call site.

### Lava Flow
Delete dead code.

## Clean code

- Use clear names.
- Give each function one responsibility.
- Keep functions short (roughly 5-60 lines of logic).
- In tests, apply DRY, KISS, YAGNI and SOLID with judgement, not as dogma.

==> .claude/rules/date-helper-seconds-to-ms.md <==
---
description: DateHelper.secondsToMs argument must not exceed 30 without explicit user permission
globs: "**/*.ts"
alwaysApply: false
paths:
  - "**/*.ts"
---

# DateHelper.secondsToMs — max 30 seconds

Never call `DateHelper.secondsToMs(n)` with **n greater than 30** unless the user explicitly allowed that value in the current request.

```ts
// ❌
DateHelper.secondsToMs(45);
DateHelper.secondsToMs(60);
DateHelper.secondsToMs(90);
test.setTimeout(DateHelper.secondsToMs(120));

// ✅
DateHelper.secondsToMs(15);
DateHelper.secondsToMs(30);
test.setTimeout(DateHelper.minutesToMs(2));
```

For longer waits, use `DateHelper.minutesToMs(...)`.

==> .claude/rules/juice-shop-app.md <==
---
description: Facts about the test app OWASP Juice Shop v20.3.0 that every test must handle (always applied)
alwaysApply: true
---

# The test app: OWASP Juice Shop v20.3.0

These facts come from the code of the tag v20.3.0 and from runs against the clean app.
They apply to every spec, page object, fixture and helper.

## 1) Quiet mode

- The app runs in quiet mode (`NODE_ENV=quiet`, file `config/quiet.yml` of the app).
- Quiet mode turns off the welcome banner, the challenge notifications and the hints.
- Do not write code that closes the welcome banner or a challenge notification. They do not show.

## 2) The cookie banner

- The cookie banner shows on the first visit. It can cover buttons at the bottom of the page.
- The cookie `cookieconsent_status=dismiss` hides the banner.
- Set the cookie before the first page load. Do not click the banner.

## 3) The language message

- Without the cookie `language`, the app sets English and shows the message `Language has been changed to English` for 5 seconds on the first visit.
- This message can cover other messages, for example the message after a click on `Add to Basket`.
- The cookie `language=en` stops the message. Set the cookie before the first page load.

Set the cookies of sections 2 and 3 in one place, for example a fixture, for every test.
Use the host of `baseURL` as the cookie domain.

## 4) Data at each start

- The app creates a new database at each start. The data of a previous run is gone.
- The catalog, the prices and the delivery methods are the same at each start.
- Do not start, stop or reset the app from a test. One app start serves the whole test run.

## 5) Coupon codes and the month

- The server accepts a coupon only in the month that the coupon names. `test-cases/README.md` gives the format.
- The server calculates the month in the local time of the server (`toMMMYY` in `lib/utils.ts` of the app). The tests run on the same machine as the app.
- Calculate the coupon code from the date when the test runs, with the local time of the machine. Never write a fixed coupon code into a spec. A fixed code fails in the next month.

## 6) Products on one page

- The page `/#/search` shows 15 or 16 products on one page. The number depends on the number of grid columns: `Math.ceil(15 / columns) * columns`.
- The window width sets the number of columns. Thus a product can be on page 1 in one window size and on page 2 in another size.
- The test case says which page or which search shows the product. Follow the test case.

==> .claude/rules/no-hardcoded-waits.md <==
---
description: Ban waitForTimeout, networkidle, BasePage.wait — use smart waits
globs: page-objects/**/*.ts,tests/**/*.ts
alwaysApply: false
paths:
  - "page-objects/**/*.ts"
  - "tests/**/*.ts"
---

# No hardcoded waits

## Forbidden

| Anti-pattern | Why |
|-------------|--------|
| `page.waitForTimeout(ms)` | Flaky, wastes run time |
| `this.wait()` / `BasePage.wait()` | Unpredictable pause |
| `waitUntil: 'networkidle'` | Unreliable on SPAs, slow in CI |
| A fixed sleep inside a helper | Same problem as waitForTimeout |

## What to use instead

| Before | After |
|------|--------|
| `reload({ waitUntil: 'networkidle' })` | `reload({ waitUntil: 'domcontentloaded' })` + `await locator.waitFor()` or `shouldSeePage()` |
| `waitForTimeout(2000)` before a click | `await button.waitFor({ state: 'visible' })` or `expect(button).toBeVisible({ timeout: 15_000 })` |
| `this.wait(3000)` | `await this.shouldSeeX()` / `expect(...).toPass({ timeout })` |
| Waiting for an element to disappear | `expect(locator).toBeHidden()` / `shouldNotSee*` in the POM |
| Polling complex UI | `expect(async () => { ... }).toPass({ timeout: DateHelper.secondsToMs(30) })` in the POM, not in the spec |

## Timeouts in milliseconds

**Never** write bare literals: `30_000`, `timeout: 15_000`, `test.setTimeout(120_000)`.

**Use** `DateHelper`:

```ts
// ❌
await expect(button).toBeVisible({ timeout: 30_000 });
await expect(async () => { ... }).toPass({ timeout: 90_000 });
test.setTimeout(180_000);

// ✅
await expect(button).toBeVisible({ timeout: DateHelper.secondsToMs(30) });
await expect(async () => { ... }).toPass({ timeout: DateHelper.secondsToMs(30) });
test.setTimeout(DateHelper.minutesToMs(3));
```

For minutes, use `DateHelper.minutesToMs(1)`. Import `DateHelper` from `@/utils/helpers/date-helper`.

## POM

```ts
// ❌
await this.page.waitForTimeout(5000);

// ✅
await expect(this.submitButton).toBeVisible({ timeout: DateHelper.secondsToMs(15) });
```

```ts
// ❌
await this.page.reload({ waitUntil: 'networkidle' });

// ✅ networkidle replaced: domcontentloaded plus a page anchor
await this.page.reload({ waitUntil: 'domcontentloaded' });
await this.shouldSeePage();
```

## Specs

- Do not add `setTimeout` or `waitForTimeout`.
- For long scenarios, use `test.setTimeout(DateHelper.minutesToMs(2))`. Add a comment that explains **why** (for example, a long checkout flow).
- In `DateHelper.secondsToMs(n)`, **n must not exceed 30** unless the user explicitly allowed it (`date-helper-seconds-to-ms.md`). For longer timeouts, use `minutesToMs`.

## BasePage.wait

- Do not write a `wait()` method in a base page. New code must not call a fixed pause.
- When you refactor code, replace a fixed pause with a concrete wait for an element or a state.

==> .claude/rules/page-object-size.md <==
---
description: Page object file size limit and component/facade split
globs: page-objects/**/*.ts
alwaysApply: false
paths:
  - "page-objects/**/*.ts"
---

# Page object size and structure

## Limit

- **~300 lines** per POM or component file. This is a guideline, not dogma.
- If a file has more than 300 lines, split it into components or move repeated blocks into `components/`.

## How to split

1. Identify a **self-contained UI block** (the coupon panel, the navbar, the saved cards list, a dialog).
2. Create a `*.component.ts` under `page-objects/**/components/`.
3. Make the root page a **facade**. Its constructor builds the components. Its public methods delegate to them.

## Example: PaymentPage

```
payment-page.ts                  # facade: payment options, continue button (~300 lines plus delegation)
components/
  coupon-panel.component.ts      # the panel "Add a coupon", redeem, the coupon message
  saved-cards.component.ts       # the list of saved cards, card selection
```

```ts
export class PaymentPage extends BasePage {
  private readonly couponPanel: CouponPanelComponent;

  async redeemCoupon(code: string) {
    return this.couponPanel.redeemCoupon(code);
  }
}
```

- `checkout-verification.spec.ts` (~1000 lines) →

  - `payment-step.spec.ts`
  - `helpers/checkout-flows.ts`

- [ ] POM file under ~300 lines, or a justified exception
- [ ] No duplicated locators between the page and its components

# Page Object conventions (POM)

Goal: one consistent style, readable code, and files under ~300 lines (details in `page-object-size.md`).

## 1) Method names

- Use `shouldSeePage()` for the basic page check.
- Name a method after its intent: `clickCheckout`, `openBasket`, `shouldSeeDeleteButton`.

## 2) Components and the facade

- Put each separate overlay or block into its own class under `page-objects/**/components/`.
- The page builds its components in the constructor. Its public methods **delegate** to them (facade):

```ts
// PaymentPage as a facade
private readonly couponPanel: CouponPanelComponent;
private readonly savedCards: SavedCardsComponent;

async redeemCoupon(code: string) {
  await this.couponPanel.redeemCoupon(code);
}
```

Example components: `navbar.component.ts`, `coupon-panel.component.ts`, `product-card.component.ts`.

## 3) Assertions in POM

- Use `utils/assertions/ui-assertions.ts` with a **descriptive message** instead of a bare `expect`.
- The POM exposes `shouldSee*` methods. Inside them, it calls `expectVisible` / `expectText` / `expectCount`.

## 4) Dialogs and overlays

- Put each dialog (for example, the product details dialog) into its own class.
- The page exposes a **public getter** for each dialog, so that specs can reach it. Example: `get productDetailsDialog()`.
- In the test: `await searchResultPage.productDetailsDialog.shouldSeeDialog()`.

## 5) Waiting (prohibitions)

- **Forbidden**: `waitForTimeout`, `this.wait()`, `waitUntil: 'networkidle'`.
- **Allowed**: `toBeVisible({ timeout })`, `waitForSelector`, `expect(...).toPass()`, `DateHelper`. See `no-hardcoded-waits.md`.

## 6) Comments

- Do not write AI-style descriptions.
- Write a single short comment only for a non-obvious workaround (for example, why you replaced `networkidle`).

# Playwright specs: no `expect` in specs

## Rule

- **Forbidden** in `tests/specs/regression/**/*.spec.ts`: `expect(...)`, `toBe...`, `toHave...`, `assert`, custom matchers.
- **Allowed**: calls to methods that contain the assertions **inside** them.

## Where assertions go

| Layer | When to use | Examples |
|------|-------------------|---------|
| **POM** | UI of a single page or component | `basketPage.shouldSeeTotalPrice(price)` |
| **Assertion helpers** | Cross-cutting or domain invariants | `OrderHistoryAssertions.shouldSeeOrderTotal(...)` |
| **ui-assertions** | Inside POM, to avoid duplicating messages | `expectVisible(locator, 'description')` from `utils/assertions/ui-assertions.ts` |

The `ui-assertions` functions (`expectVisible`, `expectText`, `expectContainText`, `expectCount`, `expectEnabled`, `expectHidden`) are **for POM and helpers only**. Never use them in specs.

## What a spec should look like

- Scenario shape: `test.step → action → should*`.
- A `test.step` contains only **actions** and **calls to should methods**.
- Make API calls through fixtures and helpers (`createCustomerWithBasket`, `basketApi`). Never use `new BasketApiClient()` in the test body.

## Structuring large specs

- Split by domain into separate files (example: `checkout/` → `address-step`, `delivery-step`, `payment-step`).
- Put shared preconditions and login into `tests/helpers/` or `tests/specs/<domain>/helpers/`.

## Exceptions

For a flaky assertion, first add or extend a method in the POM or helper. Then call that method from the spec.

# Project base rules

- **Readability**: the code must be clear at first glance to someone who did not write the test.
- **DRY/KISS**: put repeated flows in POM, `tests/helpers/`, or domain `helpers/` next to the specs (example: `checkout-flows.ts`).
- **No magic**: put strings, numbers and timeouts into constants, enums or `DateHelper` (`DateHelper.secondsToMs(30)`, never `30_000`).
- **Specs are scenarios**: `.spec.ts` contains steps and actions. Assertions are in `should*` methods of POM and helpers (see `playwright-specs-no-expect.md`).
- **POM style**: `click*`, `open*`, `fill*`, `shouldSee*`. Do not use `expect` in specs. Do not use `waitForTimeout` / `this.wait()` in POM.
- **Auth**: do not log in through the UI in regression specs. Use `loginPage.authenticate(customer)`, or a fixture that does it (see `auth-and-sessions.md`).
- **Customers**: each test that needs a customer account creates a new customer through the API (see `test-user-lifecycle.md`). There are no static users.
- **File size**: god files are forbidden. Keep a POM at around 300 lines. Split large specs by domain (see `page-object-size.md`).
- **Tags**: every spec has a Playwright `tag`. Take the values only from `utils/constants/autotest-labels.ts` (see `autotest-tags.md`).
- **Test cases are read-only**: never change a file in `test-cases/`. Refer to a test case through the `test-case` annotation (see `test-naming-no-tc-ids.md`).

Step-by-step procedures (write an autotest from a test case) are in skills under `.claude/skills/`.
Skills load when a task requests them, not by file path.

Specialised rules load through `paths` when you work with these areas:

- specs
- POM
- API setup of test data (`api-test.md`)

The facts about the test app are in `juice-shop-app.md`. That rule always applies.

# Readable code: clear at first glance

The code must be clear to someone who did not write the test. A reader should see **what happens** at first glance.

## Principles

1. **Names describe the action and its context.** Do not use `process`, `handle`, or a meaningless `doVerify`.

2. **Helper files** have one to three sentences at the top when the purpose is not obvious without them. Example: `checkout-flows.ts` (customer setup, basket setup, login).

3. **Step order matches scenario order.** The steps go from top to bottom, with no jumps.

4. **Types as documentation.** Use types such as `SavedAddress`, `BasketLine`. Never use `data: any`.

5. **Specs are scenarios. Helpers are instructions.**
   - A spec contains steps, conditions, and the `test-case` annotation. The file name and the test name contain no TC ID.
   - Each large domain gets its own `.spec.ts`. Never make a single god file of 1000+ lines.
   - Do not write explanatory comments in specs. When something is unusual, express it as a `test.step` in business language.

## Auth and customers (readability)

- A spec must not read "opened login, typed email". It must read "logged in a customer". Use a helper or an already authenticated session for this.
- New customer: `const customer = await createCustomer(api)` at the start of the test, or a fixture that does it (`test-user-lifecycle.md`).

## What to do in review

- Read the code again as a newcomer. Is it clear **what** happens, without decoding?
- If the code needs decoding, rename it or extract it into a helper with a descriptive name.

# Test naming (no TC IDs, step names)

## File names

- **Never** put a TC ID in a file name.
  - ✅ `product-search.spec.ts`
  - ✅ `checkout/payment-step.spec.ts` (domain, not TC)
  - ❌ `tc-11-product-search.spec.ts`

## Test names

- **Never** put a TC ID in `test('...')`.
  - ✅ `test('Search for a product by name', ...)`
  - ❌ `test('TC-11: Search for a product by name', ...)`

## Step names (`test.step`)

- Write every step name in **English**, like the test case.
- A step for a TC step starts with the TC step number and a dot: `test.step('2. ...')`.
  - Use the number from the test case. Do not count the steps of the spec.
  - Use the words of the TC step. You can make them shorter.
- A preparation step that is not a TC step starts with `Precondition:`.
- A cleanup step after the TC steps starts with `Postcondition:`. Example: `test.step('Postcondition: empty the basket')`.
- A step inside a numbered step has no number.
- An API test without TC steps (happy path, contract, validation) has steps without numbers.
- When a name contains an apostrophe (`customer's`), put the name in double quotes.

| ✅ | ❌ |
|---|---|
| `test.step('Precondition: create a customer with a saved address')` | `test.step('Setup')` |
| `test.step("1. Open the customer's basket")` | `test.step('Step 1: open the basket')` |
| `test.step('2. Select the saved address and continue')` | `test.step('2) select address')`, `test.step('Second step')` |
| `test.step('Response status is 200')` | `test.step('check')` |

## Linking to the test case

- Link the test case only through the Playwright annotation `{ type: 'test-case', description: 'TC-11' }`.
  Put it in the details of `test(...)` or `test.describe(...)`. Never link it through the file name or the test name.

```ts
test('Search for a product by name', {
  tag: [AUTOTEST_PLAYWRIGHT_TAGS.cart],
  annotation: { type: 'test-case', description: 'TC-11' },
}, async ({ searchResultPage }) => { /* ... */ });
```

## Splitting by domain

- Split a large scenario into several files by meaning (`address-step`, `payment-step`). Do not make one `*-verification.spec.ts` that covers the whole epic.

# Test user lifecycle

Each test that needs a customer account uses a **new customer account**. This project has no static users.
A test where the customer is not logged in (a guest) needs no account.

## Why

- The test cases ask for a new customer account (`test-cases/README.md`, "Test data rules").
- Tests run in parallel workers. A shared customer gives races in the basket, the wallet and the order history.
- A test changes its customer: it fills the basket, saves an address and a card, places an order.

## Creating a customer

- Create the customer through the API: `POST /api/Users`, then `POST /rest/user/login` for the token (`api-test.md`).
- Give each customer a **unique email**, for example with a timestamp and a random part. Generate the password in the same helper.
- The customer is a normal customer, not a deluxe customer.
- Create the customer **inside** `test()`, a `test.step` or a fixture. Never create it at `for` or `describe` declaration time.
- Never hardcode an email or a password in a spec or a POM.

```ts
// ❌ one customer shared across all iterations of a parametrized test
for (const product of products) {
  const customer = buildCustomer();
  test(`... ${product}`, async () => { ... });
}

// ✅
for (const product of products) {
  test(`... ${product}`, async ({ api }) => {
    const customer = await createCustomer(api);
    ...
  });
}
```

## Cleanup

Juice Shop has no endpoint that deletes a customer. The unique email isolates each test.
The app creates a new database at each start (`juice-shop-app.md`). Do not write cleanup code for the customer.

## ✅ Right

```ts
test('...', async ({ api, loginPage, basketPage }) => {
  const customer = await createCustomer(api);
  await loginPage.authenticate(customer);
  await basketPage.open();
  await basketPage.shouldSeePage();
});
```

# ui-autotest: auth patterns and fixtures

Part of the `ui-autotest` skill. Read it when [SKILL.md](../SKILL.md) points here.

## 7. Auth — the way this project does it (not inline in the spec without reason)

Do **not** write the login into every `test.step`. Auth lives in a fixture or a domain helper. The spec either starts from an authenticated state or calls the helper in its `Precondition`.

### Pattern 1 — a fixture that creates the customer and logs in (style B)

**The main pattern** for one connected flow of one customer.

```ts
import { test } from '@/fixtures/customer.fixture';

test('...', async ({ customer, basketPage }) => {
  // the fixture already did: createCustomer → loginPage.authenticate(customer)
  await basketPage.open();
  await basketPage.shouldSeePage();
});
```

The chain: the `customer` fixture → `createCustomer(api)` → `loginPage.authenticate(customer)`.
A fixture option (`test.use({ ... })`) can change what the fixture prepares, for example a basket or a saved address.

### Pattern 2 — a helper in the precondition (style A, different customers or states)

Use this pattern when every `test()` needs its own customer and precondition:

```ts
import { test } from '@/fixtures/pages.fixture';

// in the test precondition or in a helper:
const customer = await createCustomer(api);
await basketApi.addProduct(customer, productId, quantity);
await loginPage.authenticate(customer);
await basketPage.shouldSeePage();
```

Extract this code into a domain helper (`checkout-flows.ts`: `createCustomerAndLogin`, `createCustomerWithBasket`) or into a local function in the file. **Never copy the login block into every test**.

### What to avoid

- Duplicating `loginPage.open()` + `login()` in every style B `test()` when a fixture fits.
- Writing `expect` or login assertions in the spec. Use only `should*` POM calls after the helper or fixture.
- One customer for several tests (`test-user-lifecycle.md`).
- For details and edge cases, read `auth-and-sessions.md` (`authenticate()` versus the UI `login()`).


## 8. Fixtures

| Fixture file | Holds |
|--------|-------|
| `fixtures/pages.fixture.ts` | the page objects, the API clients (`api`), and the cookies of `juice-shop-app.md` for every test |
| `fixtures/customer.fixture.ts` | extends the page fixture with a new, logged-in `customer` |

A spec imports `test` from a fixture file, not from `@playwright/test`, when it needs page objects or API clients.

# ui-autotest: styles A and B, parametrisation

Part of the `ui-autotest` skill. Read it when [SKILL.md](../SKILL.md) points here.

## 1. Two styles of "TC → autotest"

### Style A — "TC canvas" (one step = one independent scenario)

Every step of the test case becomes a separate check with **its own** precondition (different customers, different states).

**File structure:**
- One `test.describe` per test case or feature.
- The `test-case` annotation goes on the `test.describe` or on **every** `test()`.
- Each TC step becomes `test(\`N. ...\`)` — the title carries the step number.
- Inside `test()`, put `test.step('Precondition: ...')` first. Then put the action steps and the check steps.
- A repeated flow (create a customer + fill the basket + log in) goes into a **local function or domain helper**. Put it at the top of the file or in `helpers/`. Never copy-paste it between tests. Example: `createCustomerWithBasket`, `createCustomerAndLogin` in `checkout/helpers/checkout-flows.ts`.

### Style B — "ordinary TC" (one connected scenario)

The steps run in sequence. Each step depends on the state that the previous steps left.

**Structure:**
- One `test()` per test case (or one `test()` per parametrised variant).
- The `test-case` annotation in the details of that `test()`.
- Each TC step number becomes a `test.step('N. ...')`, in the order given by the test case.
- Step names follow "Step names" in `test-naming-no-tc-ids.md`.

### How to choose the style

1. If the user stated it explicitly ("canvas" / "one scenario"), follow that without asking.
2. Otherwise, use these rules:
   - **10+ steps** with different preconditions or customers → **A**.
   - **3-10 connected steps** of one flow → **B**.
3. When the choice is genuinely ambiguous, ask **one** clarifying question. Do not guess silently.


## 2. Parametrisation (do not invent a new way)

| Pattern | When |
|---------|-------|
| Module-level `for` producing separate `test()` blocks | Same scenario, different data |
| `test.extend({ ... })` inside a loop | Scenarios differ by fixture config |
| Parametrising **a single step** in style A | The remaining steps stay ordinary `test()` blocks |
| `for` **inside** a `test.step` | Iterating over data within one scenario |
| `test.use({ ... })` | Overriding a fixture option for the whole file |

**Hard rule** (`test-user-lifecycle.md`): create the customer **inside** the body of a `test()`, or inside the iteration that produces a `test()`. Never create it in a `for` loop above the test declarations without a `test()` wrapper.

Exception: a fixture can create the customer at fixture level. A spec that uses such a fixture does not also create a customer.

# Architecture

This file is the map of the code layers. For conventions inside a layer, read the rules in
`.claude/rules/`. For the commands and the definition of done, read [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md).

## Layers

| Layer | Folder | Holds | May import |
|---|---|---|---|
| Spec | `tests/specs/regression/` | scenarios: steps, actions, `should*` calls, no `expect` | everything below |
| Spec helper | `tests/specs/**/helpers/`, `tests/helpers/` | flows that several specs repeat, test-data setup | POM, core, fixtures, utils |
| Fixture | `fixtures/` | wiring: builds POM objects, API clients and customers for a test | POM, core, utils |
| Page object | `page-objects/`, `page-objects/components/` | locators, actions (`click*`, `open*`, `fill*`) and checks (`should*`) of one page or component | other page objects, utils |
| API client | `core/api/` | HTTP calls for test-data setup, status checks, response types | utils, other API clients |
| Utilities | `utils/{constants,types,assertions,helpers}/` | routes, labels, types, assertion wrappers, `DateHelper`, coupon codes | nothing above this row |

The direction goes one way: a layer imports from the rows below it, never from the rows above it.
Page objects never import API clients or fixtures. API clients never import page objects.

## Checks that enforce parts of this map

- `npm run rules:lint` checks these rules:
  - no `expect` in regression specs
  - no hard-coded waits
  - page objects stay at 300 lines or fewer
  - no TC IDs in file names and test titles
  - no relative imports in `tests/` and `page-objects/` (use `@/`)
  - no hard-coded endpoints in `tests/` (use `utils/constants/routes.ts`)
  - `DateHelper.secondsToMs(n)` with `n` of 30 or less
- `npm run typecheck` and `npm run lint` check the types and the ESLint rules.
- No check enforces the import direction yet.

# Core beliefs

These are the principles that every rule, skill and check in this repository comes from. Each line
gives the rule and the reason. When a new rule does not follow from one of these, add the principle
here first.

## About the tests

1. **A spec is a scenario.** It holds steps and `should*` calls. Assertions live in page objects and
   helpers. The reason: a reader sees what the test does without the details of how it checks.
2. **A test that cannot fail proves nothing.** Every new test gets one mutation run:
   1. Change one expected value.
   2. See the test fail on that check.
   3. Revert the change.
3. **An absence needs a hold, not a retry.** `toPass` passes as soon as the value is right. It cannot
   show that a counter does not change later. Read the value again for a fixed time window.
4. **Zero is not a pass.** A run with 0 executed tests, or a comparison of zeros with zeros, is not
   green.
5. **The test case decides what the test checks.** When the test case and the app disagree:
   1. Stop.
   2. Show both texts.
   3. Let the human decide.

   Probe the real system first if that helps the decision.

## About the agent's work

6. **Run the check before you claim it passes.** `npm run check` is the source of truth. A claim without
   the output is worse than no claim.
7. **Measure. Do not guess a third time.** After two wrong hypotheses, add a diagnostic and read the data.
8. **Stop at a refusal.** When a guard, a permission rule or a classifier blocks an action, do not search
   for a second path to the same result. Report it and let the human decide.
9. **The checker is not the maker.** A different agent, with a different model and read-only access,
   reviews a new spec against its test case.
10. **Record the mistakes.** A log where the agent never failed shows nothing. Record where the agent was
    wrong and what changed because of it.

1	# Test cases: OWASP Juice Shop v20.3.0
2	
3	These test cases describe what must work for a customer of the shop.
4	Each file holds one test case with these parts:
5	
6	- ID and title
7	- preconditions
8	- test data
9	- steps, with one expected result for each step
10	
11	## Test environment
12	
13	- The app is OWASP Juice Shop v20.3.0 at `http://localhost:3000`.
14	- The app runs in quiet mode (`NODE_ENV=quiet`). Quiet mode turns off the welcome banner, the challenge notifications and the hints.
15	- The app creates a new database at each start.
16	- The cookie banner shows on the first visit. The cookie `cookieconsent_status=dismiss` hides it.
17	- The UI language is English.
18	- The app shows prices with the sign `¤`.
19	
20	## Test data rules
21	
22	- Each test case uses a new customer account. Register the account before the test. Each account has a unique email.
23	- The account is a normal customer account, not a deluxe account. A deluxe account gets other prices and no purchase limit.
24	- A test case must not use data from another test case.
25	- Product names and prices come from the shop catalog of v20.3.0.
26	
27	## Saved address and saved card
28	
29	Some test cases need a saved address or a saved card. Create them before the test with these values.
30	
31	| Field | Value |
32	|---|---|
33	| Address: `Country` | `Ukraine` |
34	| Address: `Name` | `Test Customer` |
35	| Address: `Mobile Number` | `501234567` |
36	| Address: `ZIP Code` | `01001` |
37	| Address: `Address` | `1 Khreshchatyk Street` |
38	| Address: `City` | `Kyiv` |
39	| Address: `State` | `Kyiv` |
40	| Card: `Name` | `Test Customer` |
41	| Card: `Card Number` | `4111111111111111` |
42	| Card: `Expiry Month` | `12` |
43	| Card: `Expiry Year` | `2090` |
44	
45	## Coupon codes
46	
47	The shop accepts a coupon only in the month that the coupon names.
48	A coupon code is the Z85 encoding (ZeroMQ RFC 32) of the text `<MMM><YY>-<NN>`:
49	
50	- `<MMM>` is the month in capital letters: `JAN`, `FEB`, `MAR`, `APR`, `MAY`, `JUN`, `JUL`, `AUG`, `SEP`, `OCT`, `NOV`, `DEC`.
51	- `<YY>` is the last two digits of the year.
52	- `<NN>` is the discount in percent, with two digits.
53	
54	Calculate the code when the test runs. Use the date of the machine that runs the app.
55	The npm package `z85` does the encoding: `z85.encode('OCT26-10')`.
56	
57	Examples for October 2026:
58	
59	| Text | Code | Meaning in October 2026 |
60	|---|---|---|
61	| `OCT26-10` | `pEw8phz3Tq` | valid coupon, 10% discount |
62	| `SEP26-10` | `q:<Irhz3Tq` | expired coupon, it names the previous month |
63	
64	## Test cases
65	
66	| ID | Title |
67	|---|---|
68	| TC-01 | Login with a valid and an invalid password |
69	| TC-02 | Add a product to the basket |
70	| TC-03 | Change the quantity and remove a product in the basket |
71	| TC-04 | Purchase limit for one product |
72	| TC-05 | Valid coupon on the payment step |
73	| TC-06 | Invalid coupon and expired coupon |
74	| TC-07 | Order with a card, from basket to order history |
75	| TC-08 | Payment with the wallet |

1	# Test cases: OWASP Juice Shop v20.3.0
2	
3	These test cases describe what must work for a customer of the shop.
4	Each file holds one test case with these parts:
5	
6	- ID and title
7	- preconditions
8	- test data
9	- steps, with one expected result for each step
10	
11	## Test environment
12	
13	- The app is OWASP Juice Shop v20.3.0 at `http://localhost:3000`.
14	- The app runs in quiet mode (`NODE_ENV=quiet`). Quiet mode turns off the welcome banner, the challenge notifications and the hints.
15	- The app creates a new database at each start.
16	- The cookie banner shows on the first visit. The cookie `cookieconsent_status=dismiss` hides it.
17	- The UI language is English.
18	- The app shows prices with the sign `¤`.
19	
20	## Test data rules
21	
22	- Each test case uses a new customer account. Register the account before the test. Each account has a unique email.
23	- The account is a normal customer account, not a deluxe account. A deluxe account gets other prices and no purchase limit.
24	- A test case must not use data from another test case.
25	- Product names and prices come from the shop catalog of v20.3.0.
26	
27	## Saved address and saved card
28	
29	Some test cases need a saved address or a saved card. Create them before the test with these values.
30	
31	| Field | Value |
32	|---|---|
33	| Address: `Country` | `Ukraine` |
34	| Address: `Name` | `Test Customer` |
35	| Address: `Mobile Number` | `501234567` |
36	| Address: `ZIP Code` | `01001` |
37	| Address: `Address` | `1 Khreshchatyk Street` |
38	| Address: `City` | `Kyiv` |
39	| Address: `State` | `Kyiv` |
40	| Card: `Name` | `Test Customer` |
41	| Card: `Card Number` | `4111111111111111` |
42	| Card: `Expiry Month` | `12` |
43	| Card: `Expiry Year` | `2090` |
44	
45	## Coupon codes
46	
47	The shop accepts a coupon only in the month that the coupon names.
48	A coupon code is the Z85 encoding (ZeroMQ RFC 32) of the text `<MMM><YY>-<NN>`:
49	
50	- `<MMM>` is the month in capital letters: `JAN`, `FEB`, `MAR`, `APR`, `MAY`, `JUN`, `JUL`, `AUG`, `SEP`, `OCT`, `NOV`, `DEC`.
51	- `<YY>` is the last two digits of the year.
52	- `<NN>` is the discount in percent, with two digits.
53	
54	Calculate the code when the test runs. Use the date of the machine that runs the app.
55	The npm package `z85` does the encoding: `z85.encode('OCT26-10')`.
56	
57	Examples for October 2026:
58	
59	| Text | Code | Meaning in October 2026 |
60	|---|---|---|
61	| `OCT26-10` | `pEw8phz3Tq` | valid coupon, 10% discount |
62	| `SEP26-10` | `q:<Irhz3Tq` | expired coupon, it names the previous month |
63	
64	## Test cases
65	
66	| ID | Title |
67	|---|---|
68	| TC-01 | Login with a valid and an invalid password |
69	| TC-02 | Add a product to the basket |
70	| TC-03 | Change the quantity and remove a product in the basket |
71	| TC-04 | Purchase limit for one product |
72	| TC-05 | Valid coupon on the payment step |
73	| TC-06 | Invalid coupon and expired coupon |
74	| TC-07 | Order with a card, from basket to order history |
75	| TC-08 | Payment with the wallet |

1	# Test cases: OWASP Juice Shop v20.3.0
2	
3	These test cases describe what must work for a customer of the shop.
4	Each file holds one test case with these parts:
5	
6	- ID and title
7	- preconditions
8	- test data
9	- steps, with one expected result for each step
10	
11	## Test environment
12	
13	- The app is OWASP Juice Shop v20.3.0 at `http://localhost:3000`.
14	- The app runs in quiet mode (`NODE_ENV=quiet`). Quiet mode turns off the welcome banner, the challenge notifications and the hints.
15	- The app creates a new database at each start.
16	- The cookie banner shows on the first visit. The cookie `cookieconsent_status=dismiss` hides it.
17	- The UI language is English.
18	- The app shows prices with the sign `¤`.
19	
20	## Test data rules
21	
22	- Each test case uses a new customer account. Register the account before the test. Each account has a unique email.
23	- The account is a normal customer account, not a deluxe account. A deluxe account gets other prices and no purchase limit.
24	- A test case must not use data from another test case.
25	- Product names and prices come from the shop catalog of v20.3.0.
26	
27	## Saved address and saved card
28	
29	Some test cases need a saved address or a saved card. Create them before the test with these values.
30	
31	| Field | Value |
32	|---|---|
33	| Address: `Country` | `Ukraine` |
34	| Address: `Name` | `Test Customer` |
35	| Address: `Mobile Number` | `501234567` |
36	| Address: `ZIP Code` | `01001` |
37	| Address: `Address` | `1 Khreshchatyk Street` |
38	| Address: `City` | `Kyiv` |
39	| Address: `State` | `Kyiv` |
40	| Card: `Name` | `Test Customer` |
41	| Card: `Card Number` | `4111111111111111` |
42	| Card: `Expiry Month` | `12` |
43	| Card: `Expiry Year` | `2090` |
44	
45	## Coupon codes
46	
47	The shop accepts a coupon only in the month that the coupon names.
48	A coupon code is the Z85 encoding (ZeroMQ RFC 32) of the text `<MMM><YY>-<NN>`:
49	
50	- `<MMM>` is the month in capital letters: `JAN`, `FEB`, `MAR`, `APR`, `MAY`, `JUN`, `JUL`, `AUG`, `SEP`, `OCT`, `NOV`, `DEC`.
51	- `<YY>` is the last two digits of the year.
52	- `<NN>` is the discount in percent, with two digits.
53	
54	Calculate the code when the test runs. Use the date of the machine that runs the app.
55	The npm package `z85` does the encoding: `z85.encode('OCT26-10')`.
56	
57	Examples for October 2026:
58	
59	| Text | Code | Meaning in October 2026 |
60	|---|---|---|
61	| `OCT26-10` | `pEw8phz3Tq` | valid coupon, 10% discount |
62	| `SEP26-10` | `q:<Irhz3Tq` | expired coupon, it names the previous month |
63	
64	## Test cases
65	
66	| ID | Title |
67	|---|---|
68	| TC-01 | Login with a valid and an invalid password |
69	| TC-02 | Add a product to the basket |
70	| TC-03 | Change the quantity and remove a product in the basket |
71	| TC-04 | Purchase limit for one product |
72	| TC-05 | Valid coupon on the payment step |
73	| TC-06 | Invalid coupon and expired coupon |
74	| TC-07 | Order with a card, from basket to order history |
75	| TC-08 | Payment with the wallet |

1	# TC-07: Order with a card, from basket to order history
2	
3	| Field | Value |
4	|---|---|
5	| ID | TC-07 |
6	| Title | Order with a card, from basket to order history |
7	| Area | Checkout |
8	
9	The basket page and the order summary calculate the totals in the browser.
10	The shop server calculates the total again when it saves the order.
11	The order confirmation page and the order history show the total that the server saved.
12	
13	## Preconditions
14	
15	1. A new customer account exists.
16	2. The customer is logged in.
17	3. The customer has one saved address and one saved card. The values are in `README.md`.
18	4. The basket of the customer is empty.
19	
20	## Test data
21	
22	| Name | Value |
23	|---|---|
24	| Product A | `Eggfruit Juice (500ml)`, quantity 2 |
25	| Product B | `Carrot Juice (1000ml)`, quantity 1 |
26	| Delivery | `One Day Delivery` |
27	| Coupon | the coupon of the current month, see `README.md` |
28	
29	## Steps
30	
31	| # | Step | Expected result |
32	|---|---|---|
33	| 1 | Open the product list `/#/search`. Click `Add to Basket` on product A two times. Click `Add to Basket` on product B one time. | The basket counter shows the correct number. |
34	| 2 | Open the basket `/#/basket`. | The basket shows product A with the correct quantity and product B with the correct quantity. The basket shows the correct total price. |
35	| 3 | Click `Checkout`. Select the saved address. Click `Continue`. | The page `Choose a delivery speed` opens. |
36	| 4 | Select `One Day Delivery`. Click `Continue`. | The page `My Payment Options` opens. |
37	| 5 | Open the panel `Add a coupon`. Type the coupon code. Click `Redeem`. | The page shows a message that says the coupon lowers the price at checkout. |
38	| 6 | Select the saved card. Click `Continue`. | The page `Order Summary` shows the saved address, the card, the correct items, delivery, promotion and total price. |
39	| 7 | Click `Place your order and pay`. | The confirmation page `/#/order-completion/<order ID>` shows a message that says the shop accepts the order. |
40	| 8 | Read the order summary on the confirmation page. | It shows product A with the correct quantity, product B with the correct quantity, the correct items, delivery, promotion and total price. |
41	| 9 | Read the basket counter. Open the basket `/#/basket`. | The basket counter shows the correct number. The basket has no products. The button `Checkout` is disabled. |
42	| 10 | Open the account menu. Click `Orders & Payment`, then `Order History`. | The page `Order History` shows the correct number of orders with the order ID from step 7 and the correct total price. The order shows product A with the correct quantity and product B with the correct quantity. |

1	# TC-08: Payment with the wallet
2	
3	| Field | Value |
4	|---|---|
5	| ID | TC-08 |
6	| Title | Payment with the wallet |
7	| Area | Wallet |
8	
9	The customer can pay an order with the money in the wallet.
10	The wallet must hold at least the order total.
11	After each order, the shop adds the bonus points of the order to the wallet: 1 point = `1.00¤`.
12	The bonus points of one product are the product price divided by 10, rounded to a whole number, × quantity.
13	
14	## Preconditions
15	
16	1. A new customer account exists.
17	2. The customer is logged in.
18	3. The customer has one saved address and one saved card. The values are in `README.md`.
19	   The shop adds money to the wallet only with a saved card.
20	4. The basket holds the product with quantity 1. No other products are in the basket.
21	5. The wallet balance is `5.00¤`. To get this balance, add `5` to the wallet of the new account with the saved card. A new account has the balance `0.00¤`.
22	
23	## Test data
24	
25	| Name | Value |
26	|---|---|
27	| Product | `Eggfruit Juice (500ml)`, quantity 1 |
28	| Delivery | `Standard Delivery` |
29	| First balance | `5.00¤`, less than the order total |
30	| Top-up for part 2 | `3.99¤`, so that the balance is exactly the order total |
31	
32	## Steps
33	
34	Part 1: the wallet holds less than the order total.
35	
36	| # | Step | Expected result |

11	## Test environment
12	
13	- The app is OWASP Juice Shop v20.3.0 at `http://localhost:3000`.
14	- The app runs in quiet mode (`NODE_ENV=quiet`). Quiet mode turns off the welcome banner, the challenge notifications and the hints.
15	- The app creates a new database at each start.
16	- The cookie banner shows on the first visit. The cookie `cookieconsent_status=dismiss` hides it.
17	- The UI language is English.
18	- The app shows prices with the sign `¤`.
19	
20	## Test data rules
21	
22	- Each test case uses a new customer account. Register the account before the test. Each account has a unique email.
23	- The account is a normal customer account, not a deluxe account. A deluxe account gets other prices and no purchase limit.
24	- A test case must not use data from another test case.
25	- Product names and prices come from the shop catalog of v20.3.0.
26	
27	## Saved address and saved card
28	
29	Some test cases need a saved address or a saved card. Create them before the test with these values.
30	
31	| Field | Value |
32	|---|---|
33	| Address: `Country` | `Ukraine` |
34	| Address: `Name` | `Test Customer` |

45	## Coupon codes
46	
47	The shop accepts a coupon only in the month that the coupon names.
48	A coupon code is the Z85 encoding (ZeroMQ RFC 32) of the text `<MMM><YY>-<NN>`:
49	
50	- `<MMM>` is the month in capital letters: `JAN`, `FEB`, `MAR`, `APR`, `MAY`, `JUN`, `JUL`, `AUG`, `SEP`, `OCT`, `NOV`, `DEC`.
51	- `<YY>` is the last two digits of the year.
52	- `<NN>` is the discount in percent, with two digits.
53	
54	Calculate the code when the test runs. Use the date of the machine that runs the app.
55	The npm package `z85` does the encoding: `z85.encode('OCT26-10')`.

## 1. Expectations (from the test case only)

- S1 (open `/#/login`): O1.1 title `Login`; O1.2 field `Email`; O1.3 field `Password`; O1.4 button `Log in`.
- S2 (wrong password, click `Log in`): O2.1 an error message says the login fails; O2.2 the login page stays open.
- S3 (open `Account` menu): O3.1 the menu shows the item `Login`; O3.2 the menu does not show the email.
- S4 (close the menu, correct password, `Log in`): O4.1 the shop opens `/#/search`.
- S5 (open `Account` menu): O5.1 the menu shows the account email; O5.2 the menu shows the item `Logout`.
- Preconditions: P1 a customer account exists and the test knows its credentials. P2 nobody is logged in.

## 2. Coverage matrix

| TC step | Expected outcome | Covered by | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| Precondition | P1 account exists | `login.spec.ts:11-13`. `createCustomer` registers a new customer through the API and logs in over the API, `core/api/customer-factory.ts:12-17`. | covered |
| Precondition | P2 nobody logged in | The browser context is fresh. `authenticate()` is never called. | covered (implicit) |
| 1 | O1.1 title `Login` | `login-page.ts:59`, `expectText` (`toHaveText`, exact) against `UI_TITLES.login` | covered |
| 1 | O1.2 `Email` field | `login-page.ts:60-61`, label and input visible | covered |
| 1 | O1.3 `Password` field | `login-page.ts:62-63` | covered |
| 1 | O1.4 button `Log in` | `login-page.ts:64`, text `/Log in/` | covered |
| 2 | O2.1 error says login fails | `login-page.ts:67-69`, exact text `Invalid email or password.` (`ui-messages.ts:3`). The input is the correct password plus `x` (`login.spec.ts:21`). | covered |
| 2 | O2.2 login page stays open | `login-page.ts:71-74`, URL matches `/#\/login$/` and the `Log in` button is visible | covered |
| 3 | O3.1 item `Login` | `navbar.component.ts:58-60`, text `/Login/` on the menuitem "Go to login page" | covered |
| 3 | O3.2 email not shown | `navbar.component.ts:62-64` calls `expectStaysHidden` (`ui-assertions.ts:16-22`). It holds for 2 s inside the menu. | covered |
| 4 | O4.1 `/#/search` opens | `search-result-page.ts:34-37`, URL `/#\/search/` and the first card visible. The menu is closed first (`navbar.component.ts:53-56`). | covered |
| 5 | O5.1 email shown | `navbar.component.ts:66-68`, the profile menuitem contains the customer email | covered |
| 5 | O5.2 item `Logout` | `navbar.component.ts:70-72` | covered |

I found no missing or partial rows. The email check in S3 has a real wait, so it cannot pass just because the menu was still rendering. The email check in S5 runs against the specific customer's email. You said a mutation of the email check made the spec fail, and the code supports that.

## 3. Violations

I read `playwright-specs-no-expect`, `no-hardcoded-waits`, `date-helper-seconds-to-ms`, `test-naming-no-tc-ids`, `autotest-tags`, `test-user-lifecycle`, `auth-and-sessions`, `page-object-size`, `page-objects-conventions`, `api-test` and `juice-shop-app`. I found no violations of them. Specific checks:

- **No `expect` in the spec.** `login.spec.ts:1-43` calls only `should*`, action and helper methods.
- **No waits, and `DateHelper` is used.** There is no `waitForTimeout` or `networkidle`. `ui-assertions.ts:5` uses `DateHelper.secondsToMs(2)`, which is within the 30 s limit.
- **Naming.** The test name and file name carry no TC ID. The link is the annotation at `login.spec.ts:9`. Step names start with `1.` to `5.` and the preparation step starts with `Precondition:` (`:11`).
- **Tag.** `AUTOTEST_PLAYWRIGHT_TAGS.auth` at `login.spec.ts:8` exists in the dictionary.
- **Customer lifecycle.** A new unique-email customer is created inside the test (`:11-13`). Nothing is hardcoded.
- **UI login allowed here.** `loginPage.login()` is the permitted exception because the login screen is under test (`auth-and-sessions.md`).
- **Cookies.** The cookie banner and language cookies are set in one fixture, `pages.fixture.ts:29-38`.
- **POM size and structure.** `login-page.ts` is 76 lines, `navbar.component.ts` is 86 lines. Both follow the facade and component structure.

Minor observations, not rule violations:

- `login-page.ts:72` passes `this.title` to `expectUrl` only so the helper can get the page through `locator.page()` (`ui-assertions.ts:44-46`). This is an awkward signature. A `Page` argument would be clearer.
- `login-page.ts:25-26,64` keep the strings `'Email'`, `'Password'` and `/Log in/` inline. This is cosmetic, and the project's own style puts product UI strings in backticks.

## 4. Verdict

**ACCEPT.** I found nothing missing and no rule violations. Every one of the 12 expected outcomes maps to a real assertion that I read in the POM and in `ui-assertions`. Both negative checks, the invalid-login error and the absence of the email in the guest menu, are real and can fail.

Optional follow-up: change `expectUrl` to take a `Page`, and drop the `this.title` workaround at `login-page.ts:72`.

I did not re-run the spec or `npm run check`. I relied on your statement that the spec runs green and that the mutation test failed on the email check.

1. Expectations (from the test case only)

- Preconditions: a new, normal (not deluxe) customer, logged in, with an empty basket.

2. Coverage matrix

| TC step | Outcome | Covered by | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | S1a: product-in-basket message | `purchase-limit.spec.ts:18` → `snack-bar.component.ts:24-26` (`toContainText "Placed Apple Juice (1000ml) into basket."` on `.confirmBar`) | covered |
| 1 | S1b: counter is 1 | `spec:19` → `navbar.component.ts:40-42` (`toHaveText "1"`) | covered |
| 2 | S2a: quantity is 5 | `spec:26` inside the loop, via `basket-page.ts:66-71` (quantity cell text and the unit price). The final value 5 is checked at the last iteration. Each click waits for the PUT response (`basket-page.ts:43-50`). | covered |
| 2 | S2b: total | `spec:28` → `basket-page.ts:77-79` (`Total Price: 9.95¤` computed by `PriceHelper.itemsTotal`, `price-helper.ts:15-17`) | covered |
| 2 | S2c: no error | `spec:29` → `snack-bar.component.ts:32-34` → `ui-assertions.ts:16-22` (a 2 s hold on `.errorBar`) | covered |

| 4 | S4b: total stays correct | `spec:39` → `basket-page.ts:77-79` | partial |

- The preconditions "basket is empty" and "not deluxe" rest on the fixture creating a fresh customer. Nothing asserts them. That is fine.

4. Verdict

**CHANGES.** No TC step is missing, and the rules are followed. Step 4 does not re-read the basket from the server.

Most important fixes:
1. In step 4, add a fresh read before checking the quantity, total and counter. For example, call `basketPage.open()` again (reload `/#/basket`) before `shouldSeeLine` and `shouldSeeTotalPrice` at `spec:38-39`. Then those checks reflect server state.

## Review of `wallet-payment.spec.ts` against TC-08: ACCEPT

### 1. Expectations (written from the test case, before reading code)

- **Preconditions:** a new customer, logged in, with a saved address and a saved card. The basket holds Eggfruit Juice ×1. The wallet is topped up by 5 with the card.
- **Step 1:** the page `Choose a delivery speed` opens.
- **Step 2:** the page `My Payment Options` shows these two things.
  - The wallet balance is 5.00.
  - The button `Pay 8.99¤` shows the correct amount.
- **Step 3:** the `Pay` button is disabled.
- **Step 4:** Order History shows an "empty history" message.
- **Step 5:** the Digital Wallet balance is 5.00.
- **Between parts:** top up 3.99 with the saved card.
- **Step 6, three outcomes:** the payment page shows the balance 8.99, the button `Pay 8.99¤`, and the button is enabled.
- **Step 7, two outcomes:** Order Summary shows the payment method `Digital Wallet` and the correct total price.
- **Step 8:** the confirmation page says the order is accepted.
- **Step 9:** the wallet balance is 8.99 − 8.99 + bonus. The bonus is round(8.99/10) × 1 = 1, so the balance is 1.00.
- **Step 10, three outcomes:** Order History shows 1 order, the right total price and the right bonus.

### 2. Coverage matrix

| TC step | Expected outcome | Covered by | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| Preconditions | Customer, address, card, basket, wallet 5, logged in | `wallet-payment.spec.ts:32-41`, `tests/helpers/customer-setup.ts:18-34` (API setup, then `authenticate`) | covered |
| 1 | Delivery page opens | `wallet-payment.spec.ts:45` → `delivery-method-page.ts:28-30` (heading visible) | covered |
| 2 | Payment page shown | `wallet-payment.spec.ts:51` → `payment-page.ts:27-29` (title text) | covered |
| 2 | Balance 5.00 | `wallet-payment.spec.ts:52` → `wallet-payment.component.ts:16-18` (`toHaveText("5.00")`) | covered |
| 2 | `Pay 8.99¤` shown | `wallet-payment.spec.ts:53` → `wallet-payment.component.ts:20-22` (exact `Pay 8.99¤`) | covered |
| 3 | Button disabled | `wallet-payment.spec.ts:57` → `wallet-payment.component.ts:24-26` (`toBeDisabled`) | covered |
| 4 | Empty-history message | `wallet-payment.spec.ts:62-63` → `order-history-page.ts:34-39` (page title and the text `You have not placed any orders yet.`) | covered |
| 5 | Wallet balance 5.00 | `wallet-payment.spec.ts:68-69` → `wallet-page.ts:18-24` | covered |
| 6 | Balance 8.99 | `wallet-payment.spec.ts:81` | covered |
| 6 | `Pay 8.99¤` | `wallet-payment.spec.ts:82` | covered |
| 6 | Button enabled | `wallet-payment.spec.ts:83` → `wallet-payment.component.ts:28-30` | covered |
| 7 | Payment method `Digital Wallet` | `wallet-payment.spec.ts:89` → `order-summary-page.ts:52-54` (`toContainText` on the Payment Method card) | covered |
| 7 | Correct total price | `wallet-payment.spec.ts:90` → `order-summary-page.ts:56-61` (items, delivery, promotion and total) | covered |
| 8 | Order accepted message | `wallet-payment.spec.ts:95` → `order-completion-page.ts:36-38` (`Thank you for your purchase!`) | covered |
| 9 | Balance after the order | `wallet-payment.spec.ts:101` (expected value is `8.99 − 8.99 + 1`, computed in `price-helper.ts:30-33`) | covered |
| 10 | Order count 1 | `wallet-payment.spec.ts:107` → `order-history-page.ts:41-43` | covered |
| 10 | Total price | `wallet-payment.spec.ts:108` → `order-history-page.ts:55` | covered |
| 10 | Bonus | `wallet-payment.spec.ts:108` → `order-history-page.ts:56` | covered |

The assertions are exact (`toHaveText`, `toHaveCount`, `toBeEnabled`, `toBeDisabled`), not just "visible". That fits your mutation result.

### 3. Violations

The rules I checked were `playwright-specs-no-expect`, `no-hardcoded-waits`, `date-helper-seconds-to-ms`, `test-naming-no-tc-ids`, `autotest-tags`, `test-user-lifecycle`, `page-object-size`, `page-objects-conventions`, `api-test` and `auth-and-sessions`. I found no blocking violations in any of them.

- **No `expect` in the spec.** All assertions are in `should*` methods.
- **No waits.** There is no `waitForTimeout`. The timeout is `DateHelper.minutesToMs(1)` (`wallet-payment.spec.ts:30`), with no bare ms literal.
- **Naming.** The test name has no TC id. The annotation is at line 24. Steps are numbered with TC numbers, plus two `Precondition:` steps.
- **Tag.** `AUTOTEST_PLAYWRIGHT_TAGS.wallet` is from the dictionary.
- **Customer.** It is created inside `test()` through the API (line 35), and the login uses `authenticate` (line 38).
- **Page objects.** Every file is far below 300 lines, and `PaymentPage` delegates to a component.
- **API.** The wallet top-up goes through `PaymentApi` (`core/api/payment-api.ts:29-35`), which calls the registered route `PUT /rest/wallet/balance` (`docs/references/endpoints.csv:12`).

Minor notes, none of which block acceptance:

1. `wallet-payment.spec.ts:29` has an explanatory comment. `readability-for-everyone.md` says no comments in specs, while `no-hardcoded-waits.md` asks for a comment next to a long `setTimeout`. The rules conflict, so I did not count this as a violation. A human should decide which rule wins.
2. `wallet-payment.spec.ts:77-79` repeats the delivery and continue actions from lines 48-50. This is a small DRY point and not a rule breach.
3. The balance checks (`wallet-payment.component.ts:17`, `wallet-page.ts:23`) compare the number only (`"5.00"`). They do not check the `¤` sign. This matches how the page renders the balance, and TC-08 does not ask for the sign.

### 4. Verdict

**ACCEPT.** Every outcome in steps 1 to 10 has an exact assertion that I traced down to `ui-assertions.ts:24-42`, and I found no rule violations. The only open point is the comment conflict in note 1. I checked the TC outcomes against the spec, the POM, the helpers, `customer-setup.ts`, `checkout-flows.ts`, `test-data.ts`, `price-helper.ts` and `payment-api.ts`.

I did not run `npm run check` or the spec. I relied on your report that the spec is green and that a balance mutation made it fail.

Я написал автотесты для всех 8 тест-кейсов, по одному спеку на кейс. Все 8 тестов проходят на запущенном приложении.

## Проверки

- **`npm run check`** проходит (последний запуск после всех правок, «CHECK OK»). Typecheck и компиляция спеков без ошибок. Lint: 0 ошибок и 43 предупреждения, все в уже существующих скриптах harness, в новом коде их нет. `rules:lint`: 7/7 ✓, baseline пустой и не тронут. Тесты harness: 9/9.
- **`npx playwright test`**: `8 passed (12.3s)`.
- **Проверка, что тесты умеют падать.** В каждом спеке я заменил одно ожидаемое значение на неверное. Упали все 8, и каждый ровно на этой проверке. Например, «Basket counter has text "2"», а на странице было «1». Или «Promotion has text "0.00¤"», а на странице «1.80¤». Потом я всё вернул и прогнал снова: зелёный. Новую проверку строк товара на странице `Order Summary` проверил так же: она упала на «Quantity … has text "3"», когда на странице было «2».
- **Независимое ревью (`spec-reviewer`).** 6 спеков получили ACCEPT, 2 получили CHANGES. Оба замечания я исправил и снова прогнал тесты:
  - TC-05: на странице `Order Summary` проверялась только сумма в строке `Items`. Теперь проверяются и строки товаров: название, количество и цена. Это добавлено также в TC-06 и TC-07.
  - TC-04: шаг 4 «Read the basket» проверял страницу, оставшуюся от шага 3. Теперь корзина сначала перезагружается и читается с сервера. Ещё одна найденная проблема: перед каждым кликом «плюс» код закрывал старое сообщение, и так можно было не заметить ошибку от предыдущего клика. Я это убрал со страницы корзины.

## Покрытие

| Тест-кейс | Спек | Шаги | Чем проверяется |
|---|---|---|---|
| TC-01 | `auth/login.spec.ts` | 1–5 | `LoginPage.shouldSeePage`, `shouldSeeInvalidCredentialsError`, `shouldStayOnLoginPage`; в меню аккаунта `shouldSeeLoginItem`, `shouldNotSeeAccountEmail`, `shouldSeeAccountEmail`, `shouldSeeLogoutItem`; `/#/search` через `SearchResultPage.shouldSeePage` |
| TC-02 | `basket/add-to-basket.spec.ts` | 1–4 | `shouldSeeProduct` (название, цена, кнопка), счётчик корзины, сообщение «Placed … into basket.», `shouldSeeRowCount`, `shouldSeeLine`, `shouldSeeTotalPrice` |
| TC-03 | `basket/basket-quantity.spec.ts` | 1–5 | после каждого клика: количество, итог и счётчик; `shouldNotSeeProduct` после удаления |
| TC-04 | `basket/purchase-limit.spec.ts` | 1–5 | количество 5, итог, отсутствие ошибки (в течение 2 с), ошибка «You can order only up to 5 items…» и в корзине, и в списке товаров, счётчик 5 |
| TC-05 | `coupon/valid-coupon.spec.ts` | 1–5 | сохранённый адрес, 3 способа доставки с ценами, сохранённая карта, панель `Add a coupon`, сообщение о скидке 10%, строки товаров и все 4 суммы на `Order Summary` |
| TC-06 | `coupon/invalid-coupon.spec.ts` | 1–5 | `Invalid coupon.` и отсутствие сообщения о скидке для обоих кодов, строки товаров и суммы без скидки |
| TC-07 | `checkout/card-order.spec.ts` | 1–10 | счётчик, корзина, адрес и карта на `Order Summary`, суммы, страница подтверждения (ID заказа из URL, товары, суммы), пустая корзина и неактивный `Checkout`, `Order History` (1 заказ, ID, сумма, товары) |
| TC-08 | `wallet/wallet-payment.spec.ts` | 1–10 | баланс и кнопка `Pay 8.99¤` (неактивна, потом активна), пустая история заказов, баланс 5.00, способ оплаты `Digital Wallet`, баланс после заказа 1.00, история: 1 заказ, 8.99¤, бонус 1 |

Ни один шаг не остался без проверки, и TODO-заглушек нет.

## Что создано

- **`page-objects/`**: 10 страниц и 5 компонентов (верхняя панель, всплывающие сообщения, панель купона, сохранённые карты, оплата кошельком). Самый большой файл короче 120 строк.
- **`core/api/`**: клиенты API для подготовки данных. Все эндпоинты есть в `endpoints.csv`, а пути вынесены в `utils/constants/routes.ts`.
- **`fixtures/`**:
  - `pages.fixture.ts`: страницы, API и cookies, которые скрывают баннер и сообщение о языке.
  - `customer.fixture.ts`: новый клиент, который уже вошёл в магазин.
- **`tests/helpers/`**: подготовка клиента (адрес, карта, корзина, пополнение кошелька) и общий путь от корзины до шага доставки.
- **`utils/`**:
  - `DateHelper`.
  - `CouponHelper`: код купона считается из текущей даты, фиксированных кодов нет.
  - `PriceHelper`: ожидаемые суммы, скидки и бонусы считаются из цен каталога, а не берутся со страницы.
  - Утверждения для POM.
  - Константы и типы, в том числе декларация типов для пакета `z85`.

Тест-кейсы я не менял, приложение не трогал, коммитов не делал.

## Для вашего решения

- **Противоречие в правилах.** В TC-07 и TC-08 у `test.setTimeout` стоит поясняющий комментарий: этого требует `no-hardcoded-waits.md`. А `readability-for-everyone.md` запрещает комментарии в спеках. Ревьюер это отметил, но нарушением не засчитал. Решите, какое правило главнее.
- **Папка `.playwright-mcp/`** осталась после моего исследования приложения через браузер, в ней только логи. Её можно удалить. Я не удалял, потому что удаление файлов требует подтверждения.
